newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait cuts H1 bad debt bond rate to 5.26 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait cuts H1 bad debt bond rate to 5.26 pct.

text.p: Kuwait's Central Bank has set the rate on bonds issued to banks and investment firms under a debt settlement programme at 5.26 percent for the first half of 1997 compared to 5.31 percent for the second half of 1996.
The average service charge would be 5.285 percent compared to 5.38 percent in the last six months of 1996.
The new rate was announced in a statement by the central bank carried by the official Kuwait News Agency late on Monday.
The rate has a direct impact on the profitability since the bonds make up about a quarter of their combined assets. It also has an impact on the state's spending.
The orginal debt of about $20 billion stems partly from the 1982 crash of an unofficial bourse and from commercial losses caused or aggravated by Iraq's 1990-91 occupation.
The central bank which sets the rate every six months paid 5.8 percent for the whole of 1995 and 5.45 percent for the first half of 1996.
According to a 1992 debt rescue plan, the rate is meant to be roughly in line with the banks' cost of funds.
The state bought the debt in 1992 in exchange for the bonds in the first stage of a rescue plan aimed at solving a problem that has enffebled the financial system for more than a decade.
